successors.note: Guelders stayed a province of the Habsburg Netherlands; the three northern quarters joined the United Provinces (the page: 'upon the 1581 Act of Abjuration') and the Spanish Upper Quarter was divided at Utrecht in 1713; France incorporated it in 1795. ledger.note: 1339: duchy. 'In 1339, the Emperor Louis IV of Wittelsbach elevated Count Reginald II of Guelders' to duke.

1379: the Jülich dynasty. After the Wassenberg line ended in 1371 the Guelders War of Succession ran from 1371 to 1379 and 'William I of Jülich won' (confirmed 1379); from 1393 he 'held both duchies in personal union' (infobox 'Jülich: 1393-1423').
1423: the Egmond dynasty. 'In 1423, Guelders passed to the House of Egmond.'

1473: Burgundy takes Guelders. 'Upon Arnold's death in 1473, Duke Charles added Guelders to the Burgundian Low Countries' (the sale was completed in 1472-73). After Charles's death at Nancy in January 1477 Maximilian ruled Guelders through his marriage to Mary.
1492: Charles of Egmond restored. 'The citizens of Guelders ... ransomed Charles and recognized him as their Duke' in 1492 (Charles of Egmond, r. 1492-1538).

1538: the end of Charles of Egmond's reign. The page gives 'Charles of Egmond (1467-1538, r. 1492-1538)'; the duke who ceded Guelders in 1543 was William of Jülich-Cleves-Berg, so the duchy changed hands in 1538. The pages opened do not state the succession year or its legal basis.

7 September 1543: the Treaty of Venlo. 'The Treaty of Venlo of 7 September 1543 concluded the Guelders Wars'; William V 'had to sue for peace' and was 'forced to relinquish Guelders and Zutphen to Charles V', keeping 'his remaining lands of Jülich, Cleves, Berg, Mark and Ravenstein'.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (3 pages; budget 5). New state: Cliopatria has no Guelders row (the Union of Utrecht row covers the northern quarters from 1579).

SCOPE. County 1096, duchy 1339, ends at the Treaty of Venlo (7 September 1543), where habsburg-netherlands (the dossier of this batch) records the matching 1543 gain with counterpart `duchy-of-guelders`. Later: the Upper Quarter stays Spanish/Austrian Guelders until 1795 (France), the three northern quarters sit in the Union of Utrecht row; those are not this state's events.

SHAPES. Geldern 6.32E 51.52N 22 km; Zutphen 6.20E 52.14N 28 km; from 1339 the gazetteer region 'Guelders' (about 9,100 km2). Gazetteer names wanted: 'Zutphen', 'Roermond', 'Venlo', 'Nijmegen', 'Veluwe', 'Betuwe' (the region 'Guelders' exists).

NOT SETTLED. (1) The acquisition years of Veluwe, Nijmegen, Betuwe, Roermond and Venlo (the page gives none; confidence-1 event at 1339). (2) 1473-1492 is entered as a Burgundian occupation; the Egmond claimants held out, the page does not say how much of the duchy the Burgundians actually held. (3) 1538: the page gives the end of Charles of Egmond's reign and not William's succession year or title. (4) The Guelders Wars page says Charles controlled 'Guelders, Groningen, and Frisia'; no Groningen or Frisia years are given there. (5) The 1581 date for the Act of Abjuration (northern quarters) against 1579 for the Union: the Duchy page does not mention 1579. (6) The page gives no area.

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: county-of-zutphen (before 1127), duchy-of-burgundy (eu-10, exists), duchy-of-julich-berg (this batch).
